purpose: Reference for reading (and rarely writing) LS-Dyna binary output via the open-lasso-python package. Query this BEFORE writing any code that opens a d3plot or binout, and BEFORE indexing any returned array. The dominant failure mode is mis-indexing array axes, not mis-calling methods. Always confirm the actual shape with .shape at runtime; the shapes below are the documented convention, not a guarantee for a specific file.

primary_imports: from lasso.dyna import D3plot, ArrayType, FilterType, Binout

file_routing.description: Map an output file to the class that reads it.

rules.note: Pass ONLY the path to the first file (the base 'd3plot'). The reader auto-discovers continuation files. Do not glob.
Pass a glob like 'binout*' to load all parts at once, or a single file path.

rules.pattern: d3plot header only / quick metadata probe on a huge file
rules.note: Reads only header bytes. Safe and fast on multi-GB files. Use before deciding what to load.
Opens transparently. Femzip is LOSSY: expect small deltas vs uncompressed. Use D3plot.compare() to quantify.

decision_guide.description: Pick the access path from the user's intent.

intents.intent: time-history of a global/section/joint/contact quantity (energies, forces, x-t curves)
intents.reason: binout stores the ASCII-database time histories; far smaller and faster than d3plot for scalar-vs-time.

intents.intent: full-field spatial result at one or more states (stress field, displacement field, plastic strain map) for plotting/meshing
intents.reason: d3plot holds per-element / per-node fields needed for 3D visualization and mesh export.

intents.intent: just need counts/metadata (n_nodes, n_shells, which fields exist, precision)
intents.reason: avoids loading state data into memory.

intents.intent: restrict a field to specific part IDs
intents.reason: returns a boolean mask aligned to the element axis of state arrays.

intents.intent: out-of-core / low-RAM extraction of one array over all states
intents.reason: keeps a single state in memory at a time.

D3plot.summary: Reads LS-Dyna d3plot (geometry + state field data). Arrays are exposed as a dict of numpy arrays keyed by ArrayType strings.

constructor.signature: D3plot(filepath=None, use_femzip=None, n_files_to_load_at_once=None, state_array_filter=None, state_filter=None, buffered_reading=False)

filepath.desc: Path to the FIRST d3plot file. None creates an empty D3plot for writing from scratch.

use_femzip.desc: Deprecated / not used anymore. Do not set.

state_array_filter.desc: Whitelist of array names to load from state data. Prefer ArrayType.* constants over raw strings. Massively reduces memory.

state_filter.desc: Which states (timesteps) to load. Negative indices count from the end. e.g. {0, -1} for first and last.

buffered_reading.desc: If True, only one state is held in memory at a time during reading. Combine with state_array_filter for big files.

arrays.desc: All d3plot arrays as {name: np.ndarray}. Keys correspond to ArrayType constants. Inspect with d3plot.arrays.keys() before indexing.

header.desc: Header instance. Use for counts/flags, e.g. d3plot.header.n_shells.

n_timesteps.desc: Number of states (timesteps) currently loaded. Note: affected by state_filter.

params.filter_type: FilterType enum member (BEAM/SHELL/SOLID/TSHELL/PART/NODE) selecting which entity class to mask.
params.part_ids: Iterable[int] of part ids to keep.
params.for_state_array: bool, default True. Matters for shells when rigid bodies (mattyp==20) exist, because state shell arrays exclude rigid shells (n_shells_non_rigid).

get_part_filter.returns: np.ndarray boolean mask to apply on the ELEMENT axis of a state array.
get_part_filter.gotcha: The mask aligns to the element axis (axis=1 for most state arrays). Apply as arr[:, mask], NOT arr[mask].

params.i_timestep: int index of state to plot (-1 = last).
params.field: Optional np.ndarray, one scalar per element (or per node). Must already be reduced to 1 value per entity for the chosen timestep.
params.is_element_field: bool, whether field is per-element vs per-node.
params.export_filepath: str, write an interactive HTML instead of opening a window.

plot.gotcha: Built-in plot handles ONLY shell surfaces; solids need surface extraction. For production rendering use the PyVista pipeline, not this. Field must be collapsed over integration points/layers first (e.g. .mean(axis=2)).

compare.returns: (hdr_differences: dict, array_differences: dict). Use to quantify femzip lossy error.

check_array_dims.returns: None; raises ValueError on mismatch. Utility for validating consistent axis sizes across arrays.

methods.get_part_filter_note: See FilterType class for enum members.

params.block_size_bytes: int byte-block padding. Set 0 for no zero-padding.
params.single_file: bool, write all states into one file.

write_d3plot.returns: None. WRITING IS RARE — only when modifying/augmenting arrays (e.g. appending history vars) or authoring a synthetic d3plot. Confirm intent before writing.

Binout.summary: Reads LS-Dyna binout time-history databases (glstat, matsum, secforc, nodout, rcforc, ...). Filesystem-like traversal via read(); tabular access via as_df().

filepath.desc: Path to a binout, or a glob pattern (e.g. 'binout*') to load multiple parts. Inspect Binout.filelist to confirm what was opened.

read.behavior: Return type depends on depth of path:
levels: read(db)                    -> List[str]: variable/subdir names inside that database.
read(db, ..., variable)     -> np.ndarray (or str for metadata like 'date').
read.gotcha: For id-resolved databases (nodout, secforc, rcforc) ALSO read the 'ids' array to label rows/columns. Data axis order is typically (time, id).

as_df.returns: pandas.DataFrame indexed by time; columns are ids when applicable. Raises ValueError if the path is not tabular.
as_df.prefer: Use as_df for any time-series the user wants to plot or tabulate — index is already 'time'.

save_hdf5.returns: None. Convert a binout to HDF5 for downstream tooling.

minimal_examples.ids: >>> b.read('secforc', 'ids')  # id labels for the columns

D3plotHeader.summary: Reads ONLY header info from a d3plot. Safe on huge files; loads no state data. Use to probe counts, precision, and which field categories exist before committing to a full read.

filepath.desc: d3plot path or buffer; None makes an empty header to load_file() later.

compare.returns: Dict[str, Tuple[Any, Any]] of differing fields.

FilterType.summary: Enum selecting an entity class for get_part_filter.

axis_conventions.n_states: axis 0 of every STATE (time-dependent) array = timestep index.
axis_conventions.element_or_node_axis: axis 1 of state arrays = the entity index (node/element). Part-filter masks apply here.
axis_conventions.tensor_components: stress/strain components are ordered xx, yy, zz, xy, yz, xz (6-vector Voigt-like).
axis_conventions.layers_integration_points: shells/tshells carry a layer axis (n_shell_tshell_layers); solids carry n_solid_layers. Reduce over this axis (mean/min/max or pick a layer) before plotting a single scalar field.
axis_conventions.critical_warning: Axis ORDER is per-array and the upstream docs contain at least one inconsistency (element_solid_effective_plastic_strain is documented as (n_states, n_solid_layers, n_solids), unlike sibling solid arrays which are (n_states, n_solids, n_solid_layers, ...)). NEVER hardcode an axis position from this table alone — print arr.shape and confirm against header counts (n_solids, n_shells, layers) before indexing.

geometry_connectivity.element_shell_part_indexes: (n_shells)  # NOTE doc row label says (n_shells,4) for part_indexes and (n_shells) for node_indexes — these two appear swapped upstream; verify with .shape

nodal_state_fields.node_displacement: (n_states, n_nodes, 3)  # ADD to node_coordinates to get deformed geometry

shell_state_fields.note: Shell state arrays use n_shells_non_rigid on the element axis (rigid-body shells excluded). Match part-filter with for_state_array=True.

solid_state_fields.element_solid_effective_plastic_strain: (n_states, n_solid_layers, n_solids)  # <-- DOC-INCONSISTENT axis order; verify with .shape

specialty_fields.sph: sph_* arrays: positions/stress/strain per (n_states, n_sph_particles[, comps]).
specialty_fields.airbag: airbag_* and airbag_particle_* arrays for CPM bags.

array_reference.discovery_helper: ArrayType.get_state_array_names() -> List[str] of all state (time-dependent) array names.

read_workflow: 1. Classify intent (time-history scalar vs full spatial field vs metadata) using decision_guide.
2. If unsure of size, open D3plotHeader first and read counts/flags.
3. Open the right class with the NARROWEST filter that satisfies the request (state_filter, state_array_filter, buffered_reading).
4. Inspect: print arrays.keys() (d3plot) or read() tree (binout) BEFORE indexing.
5. Confirm every array's .shape against header counts before slicing. Do not trust hardcoded axis order.
6. Reduce layer/integration-point axes explicitly (state which reduction: mean, max, or specific layer) and say so in the reply.
7. Apply part filters on the element axis as arr[:, mask].
agent_protocol.write_policy: Writing (write_d3plot, save_hdf5) is RARE. Only do it on explicit user request. State clearly what is being written and where before doing it.
self_check: Did I open the first d3plot file, not a glob?
Did I use ArrayType.* constants instead of raw strings?
Did I verify shapes rather than assume axis order (esp. solid eff. plastic strain)?
For shells with rigid bodies, did I use for_state_array=True and the non-rigid element count?
Am I reporting which timestep and which layer-reduction I used?

common_errors.wrong_axis: Indexing element axis as axis 0 instead of axis 1 on state arrays.
common_errors.rigid_shell_mismatch: Mask length n_shells but stress array element axis is n_shells_non_rigid.
common_errors.femzip_precision: Treating .fz values as exact; they are lossy.
common_errors.no_reduction: Plotting a field that still has a layer/integration-point axis.
